definition: a fine plaster used in decoration and ornamentation (as of interior walls)
etymology: Italian, of Germanic origin; akin to Old High German stucki piece, crust, Old English stocc stock {mat|stock:1|}

definition: a foreigner in Japan
etymology: borrowed from Japanese, from gai- "outer, foreign" + -jin "person"

definition: a dry Italian sparkling wine
etymology: Italian, a grape variety, probably from Prosecco (Prosek), town near Trieste

definition: chickpea
etymology: borrowed from Spanish (earlier usually garvanço), alteration (perhaps by blending with garroba "carob, " or gálbana "kind of pea") of earlier arvanço, ervanço, of uncertain origin

definition: a crumbly mixture of fat, sugar, and flour and sometimes nuts and spices that is used as topping or filling for cake
etymology: German, literally, something strewn, from Middle High German ströusel, from ströuwen to strew, from Old High German strewen

definition: a Near Eastern dish of ground lamb and bulgur that is eaten cooked or raw
etymology: Arabic dialect (Levant) kibba

definition: the second part in a concerted piece; especially : the lower part (as in a piano duet)
etymology: Italian, from secondo, adjective, second, from Latin secundus

definition: an Indian dish of usually braised meat or vegetables cooked with spices and often yogurt or cream
etymology: Hindi & Urdu qormā, of Turkic origin; akin to Turkish kavurma fried meat, from kavur- to fry, roast

definition: pasta in the form of narrow ribbons; also : a dish of which fettuccine forms the base
etymology: Italian, plural of fettuccina, diminutive of fettuccia small slice, ribbon, diminutive of fetta slice, probably alteration of *offetta, from offa flour cake, from Latin

definition: a flat oblong bread having a moist interior and a crispy crust
etymology: Italian, literally, slipper

definition: yellowfin tuna
etymology: Hawaiian ʽahi

definition: any of a breed of small thick-coated agile dogs developed in Japan
etymology: Japanese shiba-inu, from shiba brushwood + inu dog

definition: a usually government-operated hostelry found especially in Spain
etymology: Spanish, inn, from parar to stop, lodge for the night, from Latin parare to prepare

definition: a usually yeast-leavened bread containing raisins and candied fruit
etymology: Italian, from panetto small loaf, diminutive of pane bread, from Latin panis

definition: grandmother —used in English especially by and with speakers of Spanish
etymology: borrowed from Spanish, going back to Vulgar Latin *aviola, diminutive of Latin avia "grandmother," feminine derivative of avus "grandfather"

definition: the plain semidome of an apse
etymology: Italian & Latin; Italian conca semidome, apse, from Late Latin concha, from Latin, shell

definition: a sociable person who has cultivated and refined tastes especially with respect to food and drink

definition: trail; especially : a downhill ski trail

definition: a Hawaiian food prepared from the cooked corms of taro that are mashed with water to the consistency of a paste or thick liquid and often allowed to ferment
etymology: Hawaiian & Samoan

definition: mountain
etymology: Greek oros {mat|orient:2|}

definition: popular music of Brazilian origin that is rhythmically related to the samba but with complex harmonies and improvised jazzlike passages
etymology: Portuguese, literally, new trend

definition: day of the dead
etymology: borrowed from Spanish, "Day of the Dead"

definition: a breakfast cereal of Swiss origin consisting of rolled oats, nuts, and fruit
etymology: borrowed from Swiss German Müesli, diminutive of Mues "soft food, mush, pulp," going back to Old High German muos, going back to West Germanic *mōsa- "food, soft food" (whence Old Saxon, Old English & Old Frisian mōs "food, prepared food"), probably from *mōt-, lengthened grade derivative of *mati- "food" + a suffixal -t-

definition: a dish of fermented soybeans with a pungent flavor and gluey texture that is eaten chiefly in Japan and usually served over rice
etymology: borrowed from Japanese nattō, from nat-, of uncertain meaning and origin + -tō "beans"

definition: a robust full-bodied red wine that is known for its complexity, tannic structure, and capacity to age, that is produced in Italy as Barolo or Barbaresco, and that is also produced in Oregon and California; also : the grape itself
etymology: borrowed from Italian, regularized from Upper Italian (Piedmont) nebieul, 14th-century nebiolio, perhaps from neb(b)-, the base of Italian nebbia "mist, fog" (going back to Latin nebula) + -(i)olo, diminutive suffix (here with adjectival function); perhaps so called from a grayish film that forms on the mature grapes

definition: an Italian nobleman next in rank above a count : marquess
etymology: Italian, from Medieval Latin marcensis, from marca border region, of Germanic origin; akin to Old High German marha

definition: a semisoft creamy mild-flavored French cheese
etymology: French reblochon, from French dialect (Savoy)

definition: a rich thick vegetable soup usually with dried beans and pasta (such as macaroni or vermicelli)
etymology: borrowed from Italian, from minestra "any of various soups or dishes similar to minestrone" (noun derivative of minestrare, ministrare "to provide, serve, dish up," going back to Latin ministrāre "to serve, ") + -one, augmentative suffix (going back to Latin -ō, -ōn-, suffix of nouns denoting persons with a prominent feature)

definition: a full-bodied red wine that is known for its velvety texture, that is produced most prominently in Bordeaux and California, and that is often blended with cabernet sauvignon; also : the grape itself
etymology: borrowed from French, from merle "blackbird (Turdus merula)" + -ot, noun suffix, here diminutive (going back to Vulgar Latin *-ottus, variant of Latin -ittus, diminutive suffix); presumably named from the grape's color {mat|merle:1|}

definition: an Indonesian meal consisting of rice and a variety of accompanying dishes (such as meat, seafood, and vegetables)
etymology: Dutch, from rijst rice + tafel table

definition: a light, often brightly colored sandwich cookie consisting of two rounded disks made from a batter of egg whites, sugar, and almond flour surrounding a sweet filling (as of ganache, buttercream, or jam)
etymology: borrowed from French

definition: a smoked sausage of Polish origin
etymology: Polish kiełbasa

definition: something that appeals to popular or lowbrow taste and is often of poor quality
etymology: German

definition: yogurt that has been salted and strained until thick and that is typically eaten as a dip or spread often with toppings (such as olive oil, garlic, lemon zest, or mint)
etymology: borrowed from Levantine Arabic labna, labana

definition: a usually iced punch typically made of red wine, fruit or fruit juice, and soda water
etymology: Spanish

definition: a small plump dark green chili pepper of Mexico and the southern U.S. —called also jalapeño pepper
etymology: Mexican Spanish, from jalapeño, adjective, of Jalapa

definition: a microscopic filamentous aquatic cyanobacterium (genus Spirulina, especially S. platensis synonym Arthrospira platensis) that is sometimes cultivated for use as food especially as a dietary supplement
etymology: New Latin, from spirula small coil, diminutive of Latin spira coil

definition: spray
etymology: German spritzen to squirt, spray

definition: an unrhymed verse form of Japanese origin having in English three lines containing usually five, seven, and five syllables respectively; also : a poem in this form usually having a seasonal reference
etymology: Japanese

definition: a flaky confection of crushed sesame seeds in a base of syrup (as of honey)
etymology: Yiddish halva, from Romanian, from Turkish helva, from Arabic ḥalwā sweetmeat

definition: Korean vodka distilled usually from rice or sweet potato
etymology: Korean

definition: synthetic alkaloid anesthetic
etymology: German -kain, from kokain cocaine

definition: a deep-fried pocket of cornmeal dough filled with a savory mixture
etymology: Mexican Spanish, diminutive of gorda thick tortilla, from Spanish, feminine of gordo fat, thick, from Late Latin gurdus dull, blunt

definition: a deep-fried pocket of cornmeal dough filled with a savory mixture
etymology: Mexican Spanish, diminutive of gorda thick tortilla, from Spanish, feminine of gordo fat, thick, from Late Latin gurdus dull, blunt

definition: Greece : Greeks
etymology: Latin Graeco-, from Graecus

definition: an unfolded omelet often containing chopped vegetables or meats
etymology: Italian, from fritto fried {mat|frit:1|}

definition: a circular painting
etymology: Italian, from tondo round, short for rotondo, from Latin rotundus

definition: a cake made with many eggs and often grated nuts or dry bread crumbs and usually covered with a rich frosting
etymology: borrowed from German Torte, probably borrowed in part (with earlier spellings Tarte, Turte) from French tarte and tourte "meat pie," in part from Italian torta "cake, tart," going back to Late Latin tōrta "round loaf" {mat|tart:2|}

definition: to ooze out
etymology: Latin exsudare, from ex- + sudare to sweat

definition: butterfly-shaped pasta
etymology: Italian, plural of farfalla, literally, butterfly

definition: any of a group of often thorny trees and shrubs (Citrus and related genera) of the rue family grown in warm regions for their edible fruit (such as the orange or lemon) with firm usually thick rind and pulpy flesh; also : the fruit
etymology: borrowed from New Latin, going back to Late Latin, "the citron tree Citrus medica," going back to Latin, "the North African conifer Tetraclinis articulata," borrowed from or akin to Greek kédros "cedar, juniper"

definition: a French liqueur flavored with aniseed
etymology: French, from French dialect (Marseilles), literally, jumble, kind of pastry, from Occitan, from Old Occitan pastitz cake, from Vulgar Latin *pasticium

definition: a large bulging widemouthed earthenware vessel sometimes with looped handles used (as by Pueblo people) for storage, cooking, or as a container for water
etymology: Spanish, from Latin olla, aulla pot; akin to Sanskrit ukhā pot and probably to Goth auhns oven

definition: a lager with a strong flavor of hops
etymology: German, literally, of Pilsen (Plzeň), city in the Czech Republic

definition: a Mexican ice pop typically made with chunks of fresh fruit and fruit puree blended with sugar and water or sometimes cream
etymology: borrowed from Mexican Spanish, from Spanish, "spatula, paddle," diminutive of pala "spade," going back to Latin pāla

definition: a traditional Japanese handmade paper noted for its durability
etymology: borrowed from Japanese, from wa- "Japan" + shi "paper"

definition: a stew of fish or chicken and vegetables in a seasoned stock thickened with cream and egg yolks
etymology: Dutch dialect, from water water + zooi quantity of cooked food
